question.leadin: Since 2012, part of this body of water has been officially defined by a bordering nation as the "West Philippine Sea."
question.text: Name this sea, a section of the Pacific Ocean, where the Nine-Dash Line marks a major territory claim.
question.answerHtml: South China Sea (accept Nan Hai or Nan Zhongguo Hai)

swap.leadin: Give the following about the 1449 Tumu [tuh-MU] Crisis.
swap.text: The Tumu Crisis was a horribly mismanaged military effort by this dynasty, whose Zhengtong Emperor got himself captured by ignoring multiple opportunities to return to Beijing. This dynasty built the Forbidden City and is famous for its porcelain art.
swap.clue: The Great Bao'en Temple was repaired by this dynasty's Xuande Emperor, who was the successor of the Yongle Emperor.

question.leadin: Name some Chinese leaders of the 20th Century.
question.text: This man succeeded Sun Yat-sen as leader of the Kuomintang and fought against the Communists and the Japanese before being forced to flee to Taiwan at the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.
question.clue: This man was kidnapped in the Xi'an Incident, which led him to agree to a united front against Japan.

swap.leadin: This event occurred in the wake of the death of the reformer Hu Yaobang.
swap.text: Name this set of student protests crushed by Deng Xiaoping in the June Fourth Massacre. During these protests, students constructed the "Goddess of Democracy."
swap.clue: This event sparked by the death of Hu Yaobang was crushed by 300,000 soldiers sent by Deng Xiaoping ("shiao-PING").

question.leadin: Answer the following about alleged explorers to the New World.
question.text: According to pseudohistorian Gavin Menzies' book 1421, this explorer was the first to reach the New World, managing it before Columbus. This explorer under the Yongle Emperor brought back a giraffe from Malindi in the Swahili Coast.
question.clue: That son, Chenggong, established the "Ming Memorial Prefecture" in southern China.

swap.text: Qin Shi Huang's enormous tomb contains this group of sculptures, each of which is unique.
swap.clue: According to the Records of the Grand Historian, flowing rivers of mercury were created near the site where these works were housed.

question.leadin: George Macartney presented the Qianlong ("CHEE-an-long") Emperor with a series of toys and inventions in an attempt to end a system named for this city.
question.text: Name this Chinese city where all foreign trade was confined to the Thirteen Factories region. Traders in this city dealt with foreigners through the Cohong ("co-HONG") system, and in 1557 the Portugese leased Macau ("ma-COW") to trade with this city.
question.clue: Protesters and military cadets were killed by British soldiers in this city during the Shaji Massacre, which was a response to a movement begun in another city, the May 30th Movement.

swap.text: This leader's doctrine of "socialism with Chinese characteristics" was used to justify the creation of SEZs. This paramount leader of China instituted the One-child policy.
swap.clue: This successor of Hua Guofeng introduced free enterprise to his country with the"socialism with Chinese characteristics" policy.

question.text: It makes mention of eunuchs, the reign of Emperor Ling, and the Yellow Turban Rebellion. Chu-ko Liang is depicted as wise, while Ts'ao Tsao schemes and Kuan Yu is really good at war. For 15 points, name this work traditionally credited to Luo Guanzhong, which tells of the Wei, Shu, and Wu houses.
question.answerHtml: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [accept San-kuo chih yen-i]
question.clue: A man who later imprisons Hua Tuo is defeated at the Battle of the Red Cliffs by Zhuge Liang, while Guan Yu and Zhang Fei join Liu Bei in this work's first chapter, which sees the three of them make the Oath of the Peach Garden.

swap.leadin: From 1950 to 1970, China was shaken by various ideological experiments.
swap.text: This 1958 to 1961 attempt to industrialize China from the bottom up ended in a disastrous famine and the death of millions.
swap.clue: This program started with a focus on conserving water before moving to a massive collectivization.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Chinese Civil War.
question.text: Chiang was forced to end the first phase of the war and form a united front against the Japanese alongside the communists after he was kidnapped in an incident named for this city. This city and Luoyang were the capitals of the Tang dynasty.
question.clue: The Silk Road had its eastern origin in this city, where Emperor Qin Shi Huangdi was buried with his Terracotta Army.

swap.text: An extensive account of salt production is just some of the evidence that has been used to corroborate that this Venetian traveler did indeed visit China during the 13th century.
swap.clue: Two Dominican monks and gifts from Pope Gregory X were carried east by Maffeo and Niccolo, who were this man's uncle and father, respectively.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the career of the Chinese polymath Zhang Heng.
question.text: Zhang invented an early one of these devices, which consisted of a jar with eight dragon heads surrounded by frogs. Historians theorize a pendulum would knock a ball out into a frog mouth when the device was activated.
question.answerHtml: seismometer [or seismograph; prompt on descriptions like earthquake detectors and such]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese agricultural development in the 1900s.
swap.text: Steel melting policies popularized by the Dazhai village agriculture program caused the failure of one of these projects named Banqiao ["bahn-chyao"]. Another of these projects disrupted the baiji's ecosystem.
swap.answerHtml: hydroelectric dam [or the Banqiao Dam; or the Three Gorges Dam]

question.text: This designated successor of Mao, who had compiled the Little Red Book and was an important player in the policies of the Cultural Revolution, was killed in a mysterious plane crash in 1971. This person, the head of the PLA, was allegedly fleeing after trying to launch a coup d'etat.
question.clue: This youngest of the Ten Marshals replaced Peng Dehuai as defense minister.

swap.leadin: Identify some periods of political liberalization in East Asian history.
swap.text: Named in reference to the growth of philosophy during the Warring States period, this program implemented by Mao encouraged public discussion of Chinese policy. Lasting only six weeks, it ended with a crackdown on critics.
swap.answerHtml: Hundred Flowers Campaign [accept “Hundred Flowers Movement” or “Bǎihuā yùndòng”]
swap.clue: One element of this effort was an attempt to cooperate with the CUF and it was introduced in a speech entitled, "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People."

question.text: A group of Muslim mercenaries from Bukhara were settled near this city by Emperor Shenzhong of Song, whose capital was here. This city fell to Jurchen invaders in 1127.
question.clue: The scroll painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival likely depicts the splendor of this capital city before its final two emperors, Qinzong ("cheen-dzong") and Huizong ("hway-dzong"), were captured in the Jingkang Incident.

swap.leadin: Legends about the circumstances surrounding this man's rise to power include the "golden shelf promise" and the "sound of the axe in the shadow of the flickering candle."
swap.text: Name this man who ruled from 976 to 997 and extinguished the Northern Han to bring to a final end the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms.
swap.clue: The "Incident at Xuanwu Gate" saw this ruler take power by ambushing and killing his brother Li Jiangcheng. This ruler succeeded Gaozu, or Li Yuan, as the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty.

question.leadin: This man kept his father Ruizong on as "Supreme Emperor" after Ruizong's abdication.
question.text: Identify this long-ruling emperor of the Tang dynasty whose later years were dominated by the policies of Li Linfu. He also appointed future rebel An Lushan as a general.
question.clue: Late in his reign, he began to favor the chancellor Yang Guozhong, a cousin of his favorite concubine, Yang Guifei, one of the Four Beauties of China.

swap.leadin: This event was preceded by the slaying of a man blamed for the loss of Tong Pass.
swap.text: Identify this July 756 incident on the way to Chengdu in which an emperor was forced by his soldiers to order an unwanted execution. The victim and her family were blamed for an ongoing rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: execution of Yang Guifei [or execution of Consort Yang; or execution of Yang Yuhuan; or execution of Taizhen]
